metadata.title: Can older workers stay productive? The role of ICT skills and training

all_techniques: Multiple imputation (MI) for missing ICT skills proficiency
Logit model (for inverse-probability weighting robustness check)

confounders_identified: Industry fixed effects (if included in robustness tests)
extraction.outcome_summary: Using Korean PIAAC data restricted to full-time workers aged 16–65 (N=2620), the study estimated Mincer-type wage equations to assess how ICT skills and job training relate to hourly earnings across age groups. ICT skills (a composite of ICT proficiency and ICT use at work) and job training were associated with higher wages, with larger wage effects for older workers (50–65) who were highly educated or employed in skill-intensive occupations. The paper addressed missing ICT proficiency scores via regression imputation combined with multiple imputation, and used literacy (and robustness with numeracy) to proxy unobserved ability. Robustness checks also included inverse-probability weighting based on a logit model for computer-based assessment participation.
